newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital market closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital market closing report.

text.p: French 10-year bond futures powered higher on Friday on the back of Bunds, propelled by expectations of German interest rate easing that would pave the way for lower rates in France.
"There's a need to cut rates in France and in Germany the need is pretty well the same. They're not having an exceptional recovery. It makes a persuasive cocktail," said one analyst.

The franc was lifted from its lows by a statement by Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet late in the day that the central bank was "unshakeably committed" to the franc's stability against core ERM currencies.

The statement came in response to request for comment after two council members publicly questioned the Bank's cautious approach to cutting interest rates. After the statement, the franc was trading at 3.3972 per mark against 3.4013 earlier in the day. But it was still below Thursday's level of 3.3938.

French bond futures which closed just below a contract high of 129.20 got a further lift from U.S. Treasuries which opened higher. Analysts said they believed the French market could continue its advance early next week.
"I see a target of 129.70-80," said one analyst.
But they said key to the market's performance would be a batch of German and U.S. data due next week.

Among the figures in the U.S. line-up are the NAPM report and auto sales, due on Monday, the Beige Book on economic conditions on Wednesday, jobless claims on Thursday and U.S. non-farm payrolls on Friday.

In Germany, third-quarter GDP is set for Wednesday and unemployment data for Thursday. Industrial production is expected from Monday onwards. "The market might start consolidating toward mid-week but for the moment I see a continuation of the upward movement," said one analyst.

Analysts pointed to recent comments by Bundesbank council suggesting disappointment with the pace of German recovery as support for rate cut hopes. "There's the feeling the German situation is not that different from our own and that the Bundesbank will feel constrained to lower its rates."
That, she said, explained the Bund's strong performance. Under this scenario, the most optimistic are hoping for PIBOR to hit 97 and the notionnel 132 by the end of the year.
Both foreign and domestic buyers were reported to have piled into the French market with part of the upward movement driven by short-covering. There was strong cash buying.

Analysts dismissed the possibility France would act unilaterally to cut rates. "That would be very badly perceived by the markets. And the strength of PIBOR is a a sign the market doesn't believe that scenario," one analyst said.

Analysts said the franc now was carrying a risk premium because of the row over monetary policy but they said it was still holding relatively strong. One said she saw an outside downside risk of 3.42 per mark.
The looming end to the truckers' strike which has paralysed highway routes across France for 12 days could also ease pressure on the franc.
Only 46 out of 250 roadblocks remained across France early in the evening as drivers voted with their wheels and headed home before the weekend.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe said the drivers, who won the right to retire at 55, full pay for loading, standby and compulsory rest time and several other concessions, had "many legitimate demands." But he said many road haulage firms were in a fragile position and "a balanced outcome has been found".
